Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) – Public PDF Specification & Technical Document Links

Compiled: October 25, 2026. Scope: Publicly available PDF documents (and, for FCC/ITU/Ofcom filings, direct document records) with technical specifications for Amazon Leo, Amazon's low-Earth-orbit satellite broadband constellation. Amazon replaced the "Project Kuiper" code name with the permanent brand "Amazon Leo" on November 13, 2025, so older documents use "Kuiper" or "Kuiper Systems LLC" (still the licensee name). The terminals once called Type I/II/III (ultra-compact, standard, high-throughput) are now marketed as Leo Nano, Leo Pro and Leo Ultra.

Verification: Every link was checked on Oct 25, 2026, either with curl (HTTP 200 and a real %PDF file) or by fetching the page or document content. FCC.report, Ofcom and FCC ELS block scripted downloads with bot protection, so those links were checked by fetching the content. Dead links were dropped. Where the official FCC ICFS copy is not directly linkable, the link is marked "mirror", meaning an exact copy of the filing hosted elsewhere (FCC.report, Ars Technica, GeekWire, Scribd, planet4589).

Gaps & notes

  • No official terminal datasheets. Amazon has not published downloadable PDF datasheets or spec sheets for Leo Nano, Leo Pro, Leo Ultra or the Leo aviation antenna. Official specs (size, weight, peak speeds) appear only on web pages and press releases (aboutamazon.com, amazon.com/leo) and in conference decks. The FCC ESIM narrative (Type I/II/III gain, EIRP, radiating area) is the most detailed public terminal spec.
  • No FCC ID exists for the Ka-band phased-array terminals themselves. They are licensed under FCC Part 25 blanket earth-station licenses (E230164 fixed, E240075 ESIM). The only FCC equipment authorization under grantee code 2BKSS is the L1LA10 indoor Wi-Fi/gateway router, and its test reports cover Wi-Fi/BLE/Zigbee, not Ka-band.
  • The fixed customer-terminal blanket-license narrative (SES-LIC-20231010-02222, Oct 2023) is on ICFS/FCC.report, but no stable direct PDF link could be confirmed, so it was left out. The ESIM narrative says the ESIMs are electrically nearly identical to the fixed terminals.
  • Official FCC ICFS attachment links (api-prod.fcc.gov) work for only some documents (most return 403 to outside requests). The licensing.fcc.gov legacy IBFS links and fcc.gov document pages also blocked scripted access. FCC.report pages and mirrors are used instead.
  • No public Kuiper Government Solutions (KGS) datasheet or capability-statement PDF was found. A NASA-hosted "kuiper-brochure" PDF that appeared in search results returned 404 and was dropped.
  • Partner and reseller material (Clarus, ELCOME, MTN, Peake, Contrivian, Skyward) exists as web pages and press releases rather than technical PDF datasheets. The ELCOME press-release PDF could not be verified (403) and was dropped.
  • Canada (ISED) has an approval-list web page but no public Kuiper application PDF. No ACMA technical (apparatus/space-object) PDF was found beyond the carrier licence. The ITU SNS/SNL database entries are interactive pages, not PDFs, and only the Kuiper EPFD/RES8/RES35 PDFs are listed. The MIT DSpace copy of the Pachler et al. paper was rate-limited (HTTP 429), so the author-hosted copy is used.
